questions.question: Why can full softmax attention accumulate substantial irrelevant-token contribution at very long context?
options: Softmax assigns every unrelated token an exact weight of zero.
Each unrelated token keeps a small positive weight, and many such weights add up.
The query attends only to a fixed number of top tokens at any context length.
The residual stream adds the same learned position vector to every token.
questions.explanation: For finite logits softmax gives every position positive mass, including unrelated tokens; with long context, many small O(1/N) contributions can sum to O(1). The exact-zero option describes sparse attention, not ordinary softmax’s noise floor.

questions.question: For first-branch weight 0.5, second-branch weight 0.2, and lambda 0.5, what is the differential attention weight before multiplying by V?
options: 0.6, from 0.5 plus 0.5 times 0.2.
0.4, from 0.5 minus 0.5 times 0.2.
0.1, from 0.5 times 0.2.
0.3, from 0.5 minus 0.2.
questions.explanation: The differential weight is A1−λA2, so 0.5−0.5×0.2=0.4. Adding the branches gives 0.6, while subtracting 0.2 directly gives 0.3 because that option omits the λ multiplier. Apply the scale to the second map before subtraction.

questions.question: What key shape change lets DIFF V2 keep baseline decode speed and FlashAttention compatibility?
options: It doubles KV heads while keeping query heads and head dimension the same.
It doubles query heads while keeping KV heads and head dimension the same.
It replaces the two attention branches with a custom CUDA-only kernel.
It halves the head dimension and loads the value cache twice per decode step.
questions.explanation: V2 doubles Q heads but keeps the baseline KV-head count and head dimension, so the KV cache is still loaded once; the extra output width is projected back down. V1 halved head size and loaded values twice, slowing decode.

questions.question: At what workload does the lesson say differential attention is most worth considering?
options: A dense model with stable long-context results that is already deployed.
Any task with a short sequence and no attention computation.
Short chat under 4k tokens, where the noise floor is already negligible.
Long-context work around 64k tokens or more, where the noise floor grows.
questions.explanation: The lesson targets long-context workloads around 64k and above, where the aggregate softmax noise floor can harm retrieval. Below 4k it says the gap is negligible, so an architecture change is less worthwhile.

questions.question: With lambda=1, branch weights A1=[0.5, 0.3, 0.2] and A2=[0.2, 0.5, 0.3], what are the differential weights?
options: [-0.3, 0.2, 0.1], from subtracting A1 from A2.
[0.7, 0.8, 0.5], from adding the branch weights elementwise.
[0.1, 0.15, 0.06], from multiplying the branch weights elementwise.
[0.3, -0.2, -0.1], from subtracting A2 elementwise from A1.
questions.explanation: With λ=1, compute A1−A2 elementwise: [0.5−0.2, 0.3−0.5, 0.2−0.3]=[0.3,−0.2,−0.1]. The reversed subtraction flips every sign. The result need not sum to one because the difference is not a normalized probability map.

questions.question: A DIFF V1 run becomes unstable late in large-scale training. Which V2 change directly addresses the normalization module implicated in the lesson?
options: Normalize the gate weights so they sum to one.
Replace RoPE with a learned absolute-position table.
Remove V1's per-head RMSNorm; use simpler initialization.
Add a second per-head RMSNorm after each subtraction.
questions.explanation: V1’s per-head RMSNorm was implicated in late-training instability at 70B scale. V2 removes that module and uses simpler initialization; adding another per-head RMSNorm repeats rather than removes the unstable component.
